record.paper_title: 20 Open Questions About Deformations of Compactifiable Manifolds
record.context_brief: Compactifiability criteria for toric Calabi-Yau threefolds
record.original_question: Let X be a toric Calabi-Yau threefold. What geometric conditions on X force all deformations of X to be compactifiable, if any such conditions exist?

evidence.quote: Question 13. Let X be a toric Calabi–Yau threefold. Determine what conditions on X imply that all of its deformations are compactifiable (if any).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A complex algebraic variety X is called a toric Calabi-Yau threefold if it is a three-dimensional normal toric variety (necessarily non-compact in the strict Calabi-Yau sense) admitting a nowhere-vanishing holomorphic 3-form, equivalently whose canonical bundle is trivial. A complex manifold (or variety) Y is said to be compactifiable if there exists a compact complex manifold (or projective variety) Y-bar and a closed analytic subset D ⊂ Y-bar such that Y is biholomorphic (resp. isomorphic) to Y-bar \ D. By a deformation of X we mean any complex-analytic family π : 𝒳 → Δ over a disk Δ with 0 ∈ Δ and π⁻¹(0) ≅ X; the fiber X_t := π⁻¹(t) for t near 0 is the deformed manifold.

Determine geometric conditions on a toric Calabi-Yau threefold X (such as conditions on its fan, on its singularities, on its underlying smooth or singular structure, or on cohomological invariants) which guarantee that every sufficiently small deformation X_t of X is compactifiable. In particular, exhibit a non-trivial sufficient criterion of this form, or prove that no such criterion exists beyond the trivial cases.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up any published resolution of this specific compactifiability criterion for deformations of toric Calabi-Yau threefolds. Related literature notes that toric Calabi-Yau threefolds are non-compact and that their deformations need not arise from deformations of compactifications, but no general sufficient geometric condition forcing all deformations to be compactifiable appears to be established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Deforming Calabi-Yau Threefolds (Gross)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies deformations of (compact) Calabi-Yau threefolds; does not address a compactifiability criterion for toric CY3 deformations.
status_evidence.claim: No criterion of the requested type is given in standard references on CY3 deformations.

status_evidence.title: Deformations of Calabi-Yau manifolds in Fano toric varieties
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses CY hypersurfaces in toric varieties and their deformation theory, without resolving compactifiability of deformations of toric CY3.
status_evidence.claim: No published resolution of the question identified.
